name: Six circumcerebral configurations, CCW (Richards 2002, 2008 table)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Richards, Koren & Persinger 2002; parameter table in Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008)
summary: The lab's 30-min circumcerebral session: three burst-firing and three frequency-modulated (Thomas) configurations, 5 min each, rotated counter-clockwise through eight coils around the head with the point durations, gaps and per-coil timing of the 2008 parameter table. Persinger's lab reported about 30 % more theta power with the configuration using 20-ms rates of change, and 20 % more right- than left-hemisphere 5.0-5.9 Hz power with all six (Richards, Koren & Persinger 2002).
notes: The table (point duration, gap between pattern repeats, time on coil 1, change per coil) is from Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008, which says it reuses Richards 2002's six configurations; the research could not open that paper, so the numbers are unverified. The signs are read literally, + longer and - shorter at each next coil: BF1 runs 20 to 34 ms, the +20 rows 100 to 240 ms, the 200-ms rows 200 to 186 ms and FM1, printed -2, 20 to 6 ms, the field the lab's papers call "20+2" and reported effective in its paired studies. Persinger & Lavallee 2010 use "+" to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms for BF1, 20 to 34 ms for FM1 and 200 to 214 ms for the 200-ms rows; the literal reading was chosen because the +20 rows cannot shorten seven times from 100 ms, Cook 1999's full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms fit it better (216 ms per turn at 20 to 34 ms, 104 ms at 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published. Richards' "20-msec rates of change" probably means the +20 rows (100 to 240 ms); the abstract does not say which (circumcerebral-theta runs that configuration alone). Half of the 2008 subjects got the six in reverse order. The Thomas pulse is the exact 849-point table; the burst-firing values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst stands in (230 points; at 1 ms per point it plays three times faster). Coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2. Richards used 5-10 uT (default 5 uT, this helmet's limit); in the 2008 paired study the ring gave about 0.5 uT at its centre and 1.5 uT near the coils, with an unexposed partner in another room. military-p06-persinger-swann-1998 runs the Swann paper's version of this table (other point durations, +2 on the first Thomas row, synthetic Thomas sweep, Fpz-Oz ring). Single-lab EEG results, never independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated and blindfolded in a quiet, dark room (the lab used an acoustic chamber, subject facing south). Record EEG before, during and after if you want to check the theta claim.
schedule: One 30-min session in the original. For a self-test, compare it with a blinded sham session (the app's Blind option) on another day, with the EEG measure chosen in advance.
source: Richards, Koren & Persinger 2002, Circumcerebral application of weak complex magnetic fields with derivatives and changes in electroencephalographic power spectra within the theta range, Percept Mot Skills 95:671-686 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434867/ ; Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008, NeuroQuantology 6(1):7-21, Table 1, doi:10.14704/nq.2008.6.1.151 (no reachable copy found) ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:877-894 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738355/ ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426-436 (clockwise vs counter-clockwise) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:927-949 (Table 1, six configurations) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4) (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61-64 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/

phases.name: BF1 burst 1 ms pts, 1 ms gap, 20->34 ms/coil (+2)
BF2 burst 1 ms pts, 2 ms gap, 100->240 ms/coil (+20)
BF3 burst 3 ms pts, 3 s gap, 200->186 ms/coil (-2)
FM1 Thomas 1 ms pts, 1 ms gap, 20->6 ms/coil (-2)
FM2 Thomas 2 ms pts, 1 ms gap, 100->240 ms/coil (+20)
FM3 Thomas 3 ms pts, 3 s gap, 200->186 ms/coil (-2)
